title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure

snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and
the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded,
and then creates the ALSA devices.  If usx2y_in04_init() or
usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up
are left in place.

The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user
space may issue the same request again.  The second attempt then enters
usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still
allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or
WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb).

The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have
registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the
disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock.
Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused
with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning.  The URBs are
released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed.

A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that
path remains retryable.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect()…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close

bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents
new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs.  A rawmidi file that was
already open can still be closed afterwards, and its close callback,
bcd2000_midi_output_close(), calls usb_kill_urb() on midi_out_urb.

The URB pointers are cleared on disconnect and their accesses are
serialized with midi_lock, but bcd2000_midi_output_close() reads
midi_out_urb without that lock.  The check can therefore pass just
before the pointer is cleared, and usb_kill_urb() then runs on the URB
that has already been freed:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in usb_kill_urb+0x74/0x80
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880078e7d40
   usb_kill_urb
   bcd2000_midi_output_close
   close_substream
   rawmidi_release_priv
   snd_rawmidi_release

  Allocated by: usb_alloc_urb <- bcd2000_init_midi <- bcd2000_probe
  Freed by:     usb_free_urb <- bcd2000_midi_free
                <- bcd2000_disconnect

Take the lock in bcd2000_midi_output_close() and reference the URB with
usb_get_urb() before releasing it.  The URB then stays valid until
usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect
frees it in the meantime.  usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under
midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests

The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's
dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized.  A hwdep
file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork,
so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both
observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback
concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively.

This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index
is loaded only once.  For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits
WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may
allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice.

Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a
per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   </IRQ>

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release usb_stream_hwdep_open() and…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release

usb_stream_hwdep_open() and usb_stream_hwdep_release() pass the result of
usb_ifnum_to_if() straight to usb_autopm_get_interface() and
usb_autopm_put_interface(), without checking it for NULL.

usb_ifnum_to_if() returns NULL once the device is gone, since
usb_disable_device() clears udev->actconfig on disconnect.  The hwdep file
can outlive the disconnect: the card is released with
snd_card_free_when_closed(), so a process that keeps the character device
open reaches the driver's release callback after the USB configuration has
been dropped, and interface_to_usbdev() then dereferences the NULL
interface at offsetof(struct device, parent).  The open callback has the
same problem when it races with the disconnect.

Check both lookups and fail the open with -ENODEV; in release, skip the
runtime PM put when the interface is already gone and still run the rest
of the per-file cleanup.  Move the us122l->first bookkeeping after the
checks so that a failed open no longer leaves a stale file pointer behind.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: us122l: Add missing NULL check in usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() reads us122l->sk.s and…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: us122l: Add missing NULL check in usb_stream_hwdep_mmap()

usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() reads us122l->sk.s and dereferences it without
checking for NULL.  The stream object is released by usb_stream_free(),
which is reached through us122l_stop() both when the device is
disconnected and when us122l_start() fails, and it leaves us122l->sk.s
set to NULL.  The hwdep file stays usable after that, so a later mmap()

	KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000010-0x0000000000000017]
	RIP: 0010:usb_stream_hwdep_mmap+0x107/0x890 sound/usb/usx2y/us122l.c:182

crashes while reading s->read_size, which sits at offset 0x10.

That NULL is an expected state for this field: usb_stream_hwdep_vm_fault(),
usb_stream_hwdep_poll(), usb_stream_hwdep_ioctl(), usb_stream_stop() and
usb_stream_free() all test it before use.  Only the mmap callback misses
the check, so let it return -ENODEV, matching what the other hwdep mapping
in usx2yhwdeppcm.c does when its shared buffer has not been allocated.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer The driver uses…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer

The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated
buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync).
However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns.

If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the
send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has
updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will
observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer.

This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel
stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command).

Fix this by:
1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex
   in the synchronous command path.
2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers
   inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding
   a NULL check before dereferencing.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

title: The ITRO Popup Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_html' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.6 due to…
desc: The ITRO Popup Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_html' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable by low-privileged roles such as Subscriber when an administrator has explicitly granted that role access to the plugin settings page via the plugin's role selection option.

title: The SendPress Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'sp_firstname' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.26.1.20 due…
desc: The SendPress Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'sp_firstname' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.26.1.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The public subscriber-management route uses an unsigned, forgeable base64-encoded JSON token, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to impersonate any subscriber and obtain a valid nonce — bypassing the POST handler's only access control check.

title: The FancyBox for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Anchor 'href' Attribute in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.2 due…
desc: The FancyBox for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Anchor 'href' Attribute in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the attacker to wrap the payload anchor around a smilie shortcode (e.g., :mrgreen:), which WordPress renders as an <img> element, satisfying the plugin's a:has(img) enrollment selector and disguising the malicious link as an ordinary comment emoticon.

title: tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf.
desc:
tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf. While pulling the header bytes out of the following fragments, the loop called net_buf_unref() on an emptied fragment without first detaching its frags pointer. net_buf_unref() walks the whole fragment list, so the payload buffers still linked behind that fragment were freed as well, and the stale pointer was then reinstalled into the packet as buf->frags, producing a use-after-free and a later double free during packet teardown. The same loop also advanced to second->frags unconditionally: when the fragment still held payload after the header remainder was pulled, it was spliced out of the packet without ever being unreferenced, permanently leaking that buffer and silently dropping the data it carried.

The defect is reached from tcp_recv() via th_get() on every received TCP segment, before connection lookup or any header validation, so a single unauthenticated segment that matches a listening socket is sufficient. An attacker only needs the TCP header to straddle a net_buf boundary, which they can arrange from off-link: IPv6 extension headers are accepted on receive and their length is added to the header offset by th_get(), so a Destination Options header of a suitable length places the TCP header across the boundary of the fixed-size receive buffers (CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE). Packet chains assembled from several sources - IPv4/IPv6 reassembly, 6LoWPAN/802.15.4 reassembly, tunnel or virtual interfaces that strip an outer header, or drivers producing scatter-gather chains - can additionally present a short interior fragment that the loop empties exactly, which is the case that frees the remainder of the packet while it is still in use.

The reliably reachable consequence is exhaustion of the receive buffer pool: each crafted segment leaks one net_buf from the fixed CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX_COUNT pool, the buffers are never reclaimed, and once the pool is empty the device can no longer receive network traffic until it is rebooted. Where a fragment is emptied exactly, the impact rises to memory corruption: freed pool buffers are written through by the remainder of the loop, their contents may be delivered to the application, and the packet is double-freed on teardown.

The fix saves and clears second->frags before the net_buf_unref() so only the emptied header fragment is released, and advances to the next fragment only when second->len == 0, keeping any fragment that still holds payload in the packet. This restores the detach-before-unref ownership pattern used elsewhere in the stack, for example in net_pkt_trim_buffer().

title: Issue summary: Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments may cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly buffer for each buffered message, so a…
desc:
Issue summary: Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments may
cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly buffer for each
buffered message, so a small amount of wire data consumes a large amount of
memory.

Impact summary: A remote attacker can send a few small crafted DTLS handshake
fragments to make a DTLS server or client allocate well over a megabyte of
memory per connection, which may lead to memory exhaustion and Denial of
Service if many connections are made.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: DTLS handshake messages can arrive out of order and fragmented,
so OpenSSL buffers fragments of up to ten out-of-sequence messages until
reassembly is possible. When the first fragment of a new message arrives,
OpenSSL allocates a buffer sized to the full message length declared in the
fragment header, plus a reassembly bitmap, instead of storing only the bytes
actually received. The declared length is capped by the maximum certificate
list size, 128KB by default, and that cap applies to every handshake message
type rather than only to Certificate messages.

Only DTLS endpoints reach this code. TLS, QUIC and applications that do not
use DTLS are unaffected. An attacker sends fragments that declare a large
message length but carry almost no data, using up to ten distinct message
sequence numbers.

A single connection can then hold roughly 1.4MB of buffers from about 156
bytes on the wire. Because the number of buffered messages is capped, memory
exhaustion requires many connections or many peers, which is why the severity
is Low.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

desc:
Use of externally-controlled format string in certain ASUS Router firmware allows a nearby administrator to read or write memory, potentially resulting in a denial-of-service, via crafted format specifiers sent to the logging/summary function.
Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

title: Insertion of sensitive information into sent data in certain ASUS Router firmware allows a remote attacker to obtain router’s UID or login authorization tokens for the victim's…
desc:
Insertion of sensitive information into sent data in certain ASUS Router firmware allows a remote attacker to obtain router’s UID or login authorization tokens for the victim's linked account via a crafted web page, which requires a logged-in router administrator to actively complete the third-party authorization flow.
Refer to the '
Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

title: The Make Connector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.6 via the include_custom_fields.
desc: The Make Connector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.6 via the include_custom_fields. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract arbitrary admin-selected user, post, comment, and term metadata exposed via core REST endpoints — including active session tokens with source IP, user-agent, login and expiry timestamps, capability sets, and any other admin-selected private meta keys including protected underscore-prefixed entries. This is exploitable because the plugin's meta picker queries all meta keys from the database without filtering, offering protected underscore-prefixed keys such as session_tokens and wp_capabilities for administrator selection; if any such keys are selected, their values become readable without any credentials.

title: The Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via 'wpacu_unload_css' and 'wpacu_unload_js' Query Parameters in all…
desc: The Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via 'wpacu_unload_css' and 'wpacu_unload_js' Query Parameters in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.0.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation requires that the victim has sufficient privileges to see the plugin's admin-bar entry, typically an administrator.

title: Netgate pfSense CE XMLRPC Incorrect Authorization Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
desc:
Netgate pfSense CE XMLRPC Incorrect Authorization Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Netgate pfSense. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the XMLRPC endpoint. The issue results from incorrect authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code within the context of the root. Was ZDI-CAN-32353.

title: Vulnerability in the Oracle WebCenter Content product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Content Portal Suite).
desc: Vulnerability in the Oracle WebCenter Content product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Content Portal Suite).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle WebCenter Content.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle WebCenter Content accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.1 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

title: ** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation.
desc:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Alternatively you could use a build of Axis with the patch from https://github.com/apache/axis-axis1-java/commit/41f3b4e8d04e310ca81f86b92630ab2c11d608bd applied. The Apache Axis project does not expect to create an Axis 1.x release fixing this problem.

title: Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA records.
desc:
Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL
pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA
records.

Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash (potential Denial
of Service).

CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference

Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA records with at
least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside the DANE-TA(2)
usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the server claims a trusted
CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has an unusual mix of
associated TLSA records.

DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the
DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified applicable
in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected, while the Exim
MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE implementation.

Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys (RPKs) is also
unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.

Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with a traditional PKI
are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or similar, that uses
OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.

FIPS impact: no
The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.

title: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics.
desc: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/import handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py accepts a ZIP archive and moves an included database file to DATABASE_PATH while also replacing IMAGE_PATH content. An attacker can supply a database containing an attacker-controlled users table and administrative account, then authenticate as that account; invalid replacement data can also destroy application data or availability. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

title: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics.
desc: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/images/manga/save handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/image.py accepts a client-controlled filename and joins it to IMAGE_SAVE_PATH without confining the result. Traversal sequences can escape the image directory and overwrite process-writable files, including DATABASE_PATH for the live SQLite database, while the client-supplied image content type does not validate the uploaded bytes. An attacker can replace the database to plant an administrative user and can overwrite other writable files, causing full application compromise and availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

title: OwnPay is a self-hosted open-source payment gateway automation platform.
desc: OwnPay is a self-hosted open-source payment gateway automation platform. In 0.2.0 and earlier, modules/gateways/alipay/AlipayGateway.php fails open when an Alipay callback lacks a signature or the merchant has no configured public key because verify(array $callbackData, array $credentials) falls back to an undefined mode credential that defaults to test mode, while verifyWebhook() returns true unconditionally. An unauthenticated request to POST /webhook/{gateway} can provide a pending order reference and matching amount, pass both verification gates without a valid payment signature, and cause the order and corresponding payment-received ledger entries to be marked completed. No fixed version is available as of this review.

title: IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information and perform unauthorized actions due to improper validation of a redirect…
desc: IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information and perform unauthorized actions due to improper validation of a redirect URL.

title: The Edwiser Bridge WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 does not correctly scope one of its REST API authentication checks, disabling WordPress's REST nonce validation for every route…
desc: The Edwiser Bridge  WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 does not correctly scope one of its REST API authentication checks, disabling WordPress's REST nonce validation for every route on the site, which allows attackers to make a logged-in administrator perform arbitrary privileged actions, such as creating a new administrator account, via CSRF.

title: yt-mcp is a YouTrack MCP server for Claude Code.
desc: yt-mcp is a YouTrack MCP server for Claude Code. Prior to 1.18.1, add_attachment in src/yt_mcp/tools/attachments.py accepts a caller-controlled file_path, checks only that the file exists, reads it without directory confinement, and uploads the bytes to a YouTrack issue. A compromised MCP client or an LLM steered by indirect prompt injection can read any file accessible to the server process and exfiltrate secrets through an issue the caller can access. The same release also permits get_project_health to interpolate a caller-controlled project value into snapshot filenames, allowing parent-directory traversal to write JSON files outside the snapshots directory. This issue is fixed in version 1.18.1.

title: OliveTin gives safe and simple access to predefined shell commands from a web interface.
desc: OliveTin gives safe and simple access to predefined shell commands from a web interface. From 3000.0.0 until 3000.18.1, OliveTin passes attacker-influenceable output and ot_username values into shellAfterCompleted processing in service/internal/executor/executor.go without applying checkShellArgumentSafety, the shell-safety validation used for primary action execution. The same post-execution template path also expands exitCode without that validation, but the advisory does not establish attacker control of the exit-code value. When an action configures shellAfterCompleted with output or ot_username, shell metacharacters from command output, external data processed by an action, or a trusted-header username can become syntax in the command executed by the stepExecAfter path. This can execute arbitrary commands as the OliveTin process user, including when the primary action uses the safer exec-array mode. This issue is fixed in version 3000.18.1.

title: Music Assistant is an open-source media library manager that integrates streaming services with connected speakers.
desc: Music Assistant is an open-source media library manager that integrates streaming services with connected speakers. Prior to 2.8.0, parse_arguments() passes the caller-controlled return_type parameter for config/core/get_value, config/providers/get_value, and config/players/get_value to parse_value() and Python eval() when resolving type parameters in music_assistant/helpers/api.py. Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can reach these commands through the WebSocket /ws endpoint or the REST JSON-RPC /api endpoint, causing arbitrary Python code to run with the Music Assistant server process privileges before command-handler validation, even if the request later fails. A default installation requires no special configuration, and compromise can expose secrets and configuration, alter library data, and control the application container. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

title: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms.
desc: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms uses a public hard-coded fallback JWT signing secret from server/config/auth.config.js when ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is unset. An unauthenticated attacker can sign a self-contained token with privileged claims because server/src/auth/auth_jwt.js verifies the signature without reloading the user from the database, and server/src/lib/middleware.js trusts the token's roles and options for authorization. A forged token can therefore be accepted as an administrator session, resulting in authentication bypass and full privileged API access. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

title: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms.
desc: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms allows a user with repository management privileges to inject shell syntax through repository uri, branch, name, or host values processed by server/src/models/repo.model.js. The Repo.clone and Repo.addKnownHosts paths interpolate these values into git and ssh-keyscan command strings, and server/src/lib/cmd.js executes the strings through Cmd.executeSilentCommand with shell interpretation enabled. Creating or updating a repository can therefore execute arbitrary commands as the AnsibleForms application process. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

title: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms.
desc: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms stores attacker-influenceable job output that server/src/lib/common.js processes through formatOutput without HTML escaping and client/src/components/AppAnsibleOutput.vue renders through v-html. An authenticated user can submit job input that is echoed into persistent output, causing script execution when another user views the job. Additional designer-controlled HTML and expression values reach v-html in client/src/components/AppForm.vue and client/src/components/BsInputForForm.vue without sanitization. Because Content Security Policy is disabled and the JWT is stored in localStorage, script execution can steal a victim's token and take over the account, including an administrator account. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

title: install-artifact-from-github installs prebuilt native artifacts hosted by GitHub without compiling them locally.
desc: install-artifact-from-github installs prebuilt native artifacts hosted by GitHub without compiling them locally. Prior to 1.7.0, bin/install-from-cache.js downloads a native .node artifact, allows RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR to select a source, follows HTTP redirects including HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrades, and writes the decompressed response to the artifact path without cryptographic integrity verification before writing or loading it. An attacker who controls a configured mirror, replaces a release asset, or can modify plaintext transport can supply native code that executes when the consumer loads the artifact. Version 1.7.0 adds SHA-256 verification for default-GitHub-source downloads when the consuming package publishes an artifactHashes bag; configured mirrors and packages without a bag remain outside that verification.

title: The Chainguard SDK is a public Go SDK for integrating with the Chainguard platform.
desc: The Chainguard SDK is a public Go SDK for integrating with the Chainguard platform. Prior to 0.1.107, auth/aws.VerifyToken trusts the Chainguard-Audience and Chainguard-Identity headers without requiring those headers to be covered by AWS SigV4 SignedHeaders. An attacker with a fresh STS GetCallerIdentity request signed by a victim can rewrite the unsigned binding headers and replay the proof to another relying party, causing the relying party to authenticate the victim’s AWS identity for an attacker-chosen audience and identity. Code that only uses auth/aws.GenerateToken is unaffected because the generator signs the binding headers, and exploitation requires a signed request within its validity window. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.107.

title: cf-manager is an all-in-one dashboard for managing multiple Cloudflare accounts and services.
desc: cf-manager is an all-in-one dashboard for managing multiple Cloudflare accounts and services. Prior to 1.1.2, worker/src/routes/workers.ts uses bare fetch(url) calls to retrieve user-supplied URLs and deploys the returned content as a Worker script using stored Cloudflare credentials. The multipart and JSON branches of POST /api/:accountId/workers and POST /api/batch-deploy accept URLs without protocol, destination, redirect, content-type, or response-size validation. An attacker with deployment API access, or unauthenticated access when API_SECRET is not configured, can make cf-manager access internal resources or fetch attacker-controlled JavaScript and execute it in the victim Cloudflare Workers account. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.2.

title: ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges.
desc: ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when a challenge payload omits the signature field, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker can remove the signature, supply attacker-selected low-difficulty challenge parameters, solve the resulting proof of work, and submit a payload that verifies successfully, bypassing the CAPTCHA control. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

title: WPGraphQL Content Blocks is a WordPress plugin that extends WPGraphQL to support querying Gutenberg blocks as data.
desc: WPGraphQL Content Blocks is a WordPress plugin that extends WPGraphQL to support querying Gutenberg blocks as data. Prior to 4.8.6, the editorBlocks renderedHtml field in includes/Data/ContentBlocksResolver.php uses resolve_content_blocks() to read a post with get_post() without applying post_password_required(). An unauthenticated caller who knows a supported post identifier can therefore retrieve the complete body of a password-protected published post without a post password, nonce, or valid cookie, exposing paid, member-only, preview, or internal content. This issue is fixed in version 4.8.6.

title: Outstatic is a static site CMS for Markdown and MDX content stored in GitHub repositories.
desc: Outstatic is a static site CMS for Markdown and MDX content stored in GitHub repositories. Prior to 2.2.1, the authenticated GitHub REST proxy accepts an unvalidated endpoint value, constructs an upstream URL by string concatenation, and attaches the current dashboard user's GitHub OAuth token without ensuring the destination remains the exact GitHub API origin. An authenticated dashboard user can cause the server to send that user's token to a non-GitHub host, potentially exposing private repositories and other resources allowed by the token's scopes. The issue does not let an unauthenticated attacker access private data and does not directly expose another user's token without an additional same-origin execution or request-forging primitive. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.1.

title: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database.
desc: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. Prior to 0.40.3, unauthenticated requests to /bookmark can supply a url that server/src/plugins/bookmark.rs passes through fetch_data to fetch_body. Endpoint dispatch in lib/src/db.rs invokes the handler before check_read, and lib/src/client/helpers.rs previously checked only that the URL began with HTTP, without restricting loopback, private, link-local, DNS-rebinding, or redirect targets. The handler reflects fetched content in returned resource fields, making this a full-response server-side request forgery that can expose internal services and plain-GET cloud metadata. The short request timeout limits slow targets, and metadata services requiring a separate token request are outside the demonstrated GET-only path. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

title: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database.
desc: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.29.0 to 0.40.2, Atomic Server provisions a well-known /setup invite with write enabled, the Drive root as its target, and usagesLeft set to one. construct_invite_redirect in server/src/plugins/invite.rs discards the redeemer identity, so an unauthenticated request containing an attacker-controlled public-key can create a new Agent and grant it write access to the entire Drive. On a fresh, unclaimed deployment, this permits reading, modifying, or deleting resources, changing permissions, and creating or altering Agents. No complete fixed version was verified as of this review.

title: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database.
desc: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, the Commit application path in lib/src/commit.rs allows an authenticated Agent to assign the server-managed internalId property to an owned resource without character validation. The /download handler in server/src/handlers/download.rs passes that value to filesystem path construction and NamedFile::open without sanitization, containment validation, or a File-class check, so traversal or absolute paths can read files available to the server process. Reading the server configuration can expose the root Agent private key and allow root impersonation with full read, write, and delete access to server data. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

title: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database.
desc: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, an authenticated Agent with folder write access can use POST /upload to store HTML or SVG content that GET /download/{path} serves from the application origin through server/src/handlers/download.rs. The response sets Content-Disposition: inline and lacks forced attachment handling and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, allowing the browser to render the uploaded active content as the application. When a victim opens the link, the script can access the JavaScript-readable atomic_session cookie and the Agent private key in same-origin IndexedDB, enabling persistent account impersonation. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

title: djangocms-versioning is a general-purpose versioning package for django CMS 4 and later.
desc: djangocms-versioning is a general-purpose versioning package for django CMS 4 and later. Prior to 2.6.1, the check_discard and check_edit_redirect Conditions on djangocms_versioning.models.Version omit user_can_change, while VersionAdmin.discard_view and VersionAdmin.edit_redirect_view obtain a version by its primary key and rely on those conditions for object-level authorization. With CMS_PERMISSION set to True, the affected views are gated only by is_staff, allowing any staff user to select content without object-level change permission. With the default CMS_PERMISSION value of False, a staff user must also hold the global Django change_ permission, but that model-level permission does not enforce the intended per-object authorization, so the user can delete a draft version and its content object through discard or create an editable draft from a published version through edit_redirect even when the user cannot change that specific content object. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.1.

title: django-filer is a file and image management application for Django.
desc: django-filer is a file and image management application for Django. Prior to 3.5.0, the delete_files_or_folders action in filer/admin/folderadmin.py checks global Django model-level deletion permission but omits check_folder_edit_permissions and check_files_edit_permissions when FILER_ENABLE_PERMISSIONS is enabled. An authenticated staff user who has a global delete_file, delete_folder, or delete_image permission but is limited to read-only access by FolderPermission can therefore delete files, folders, and descendants from the restricted folder. Deployments using the default disabled per-folder permission system are not affected, and the issue does not create a read-confidentiality impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.5.0.

title: LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware.
desc: LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

title: QPixel is a Q&A-based community knowledge-sharing software.
desc: QPixel is a Q&A-based community knowledge-sharing software. Prior to 0.13.0, the unauthenticated comments#show action in app/controllers/comments_controller.rb resolves user-controlled comment IDs with Comment.unscoped, bypassing the Comment community default scope, and performs no deletion or post-visibility authorization check. A remote unauthenticated attacker can enumerate sequential IDs and read the full content of comments belonging to other communities, soft-deleted comments, and comments under access-restricted categories. The JSON response exposes the stored comment columns because the model has no limiting as_json override. This issue is fixed in version 0.13.0.

title: augment-vir is a collection of helper functions.
desc: augment-vir is a collection of helper functions. Prior to version 31.73.5, the grep() function exported by @augment-vir/node inserts caller-controlled search patterns directly into a double-quoted shell command string without sanitization (grep.ts:310). When the constructed command is passed to spawn() with shell: 'bash' (shell.ts:98-99), bash evaluates $() command substitution expressions embedded in the pattern, resulting in arbitrary OS command execution as the Node.js process user. Any downstream application that passes untrusted input to grep()'s pattern or patterns field is vulnerable to unauthenticated local (and potentially remote) code execution. This issue has been patched in version 31.73.5.

title: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software.
desc: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2 and 7.7.3, the Configuration Proxy uses attacker-controlled Content-location metadata from a validly signed federated global configuration part when constructing an output path without verifying that the resulting path remains inside the intended configuration output directory. A malicious or compromised federated ecosystem can provide an absolute path or directory traversal sequence during the normal refresh cycle, causing the Configuration Proxy to create a new file with attacker-controlled content under the permissions of the non-privileged xroad process. The vulnerability can poison downstream global configuration or create files in other writable locations, but it does not overwrite existing files. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2 and 7.7.3.

title: Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots.
desc: Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots. Prior to 1.11.5, the unauthenticated GET /api/v1/view/* route in server/src/routes/api/v1/view/root.ts resolves its attacker-controlled wildcard path without normalization or containment, allowing traversal outside the intended uploads directory and arbitrary server file reads. Reading environment files can disclose DB_SECRET_KEY, the application’s JWT signing key, which permits forged administrator tokens and takeover of bots, conversations, integrations, and stored third-party credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.5.

title: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software.
desc: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to .8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.5, the Security Server writes each downloaded federated global-configuration part under the X-Road instance identifier declared by the part itself without checking that the identifier matches the source ecosystem that signed and delivered it. A malicious or compromised federated ecosystem can provide a validly signed SHARED-PARAMETERS part naming a victim ecosystem, causing the part to be written as the victim's authoritative shared-params.xml. The poisoned configuration can persist across refreshes, add attacker-controlled trust material, and enable impersonation of victim members and Security Servers across every ecosystem federated with the malicious source. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.5.

title: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software.
desc: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4, HashChainVerifier in the common-message module resolves attacker-controlled batch-signature hash chains before verifying the message signature and signing certificate, without cycle detection, recursion-depth or total-step limits, or per-step memoization. A registered ecosystem member can send a small crafted hashchain MIME part with repeated or cyclic StepRef values so that verifyHashChain() performs exponential work or unbounded recursion before authentication. Repeated requests can exhaust Security Server proxy threads and deny data-exchange service, and a self-reference can raise an uncaught error. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4.

title: SNARK Verifier is a generic (S)NARK verifier.
desc: SNARK Verifier is a generic (S)NARK verifier. Prior to 0.2.5, KZG accumulator public-instance limbs are decoded without consistently enforcing canonical limb bounds before elliptic-curve coordinate reconstruction. `PlonkProof::read` selects scalars using `accumulator_indices` and passes them to `AccumulatorEncoding::from_repr`. For the EVM loader, `LimbsEncoding::from_repr` forwards them to `EvmLoader::ec_point_from_limbs` in `snark-verifier/src/loader/evm/loader.rs`, where `shl` and `add` reconstruct coordinates before `validate_ec_point` checks the resulting affine point rather than the original limb bounds. The related native path in `snark-verifier/src/pcs/kzg/accumulator.rs` can reach assertion- or unwrap-based decoding and panic instead of returning a verification error. This allows noncanonical encodings at the verifier boundary and can crash the native verifier. Standard SDK aggregation circuits are expected to constrain accumulator limbs before this boundary, which limits practical exploitability. This issue is fixed in version 0.2.5.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/record_audio_rtc.ajax.php concatenates the user-controlled audio_dir parameter with the course document root and passes the result to recursive directory creation without path normalization. An authenticated course user can select directory paths outside the intended course storage tree wherever the web-server account has permission to create directories. The resulting filesystem changes can interfere with application layout or support a separate file-write or code-execution chain, although this endpoint alone is not shown to write attacker-selected file content outside the course tree. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/dropbox/dropbox_functions.inc.php accepts a literal .htaccess filename in the course dropbox and stores it in a directory served by Apache, where the file can alter handler behavior under the required AllowOverride All configuration. Any authenticated course participant can upload .htaccess and then upload a PHP payload disguised as a .gif, resulting in code execution as the web-server user when the dropbox tool is enabled. This can expose or modify the Chamilo installation, course content, and database credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/user_manager.ajax.php exposes the update_users action without an authorization check and stores attacker-controlled firstname, lastname, and email values without HTML sanitization. An unauthenticated attacker can modify another user's profile fields, and the stored content executes when user_portal.php, the administrative user listing, user information, social profile, course participant list, or message-composer recipient header renders the modified account. Targeting an administrator account can expose administrator-session data or permit actions in that session. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

title: The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog.
desc: The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line and in 2.0.0, plugin/cleandeletedfiles/src/ajax.php and public/plugin/CleanDeletedFiles/src/ajax.php pass the request path parameter and list parameter directly to unlink without canonicalization, filename validation, or confinement to the plugin's scanned directories. An authenticated administrator can delete arbitrary files writable by the web server; a cross-site request forgery against an administrator session can reach the same operation. Deleting application source, uploaded content, cache, or configuration files can cause data loss and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line. No fixed 2.0 release is established as of this review.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, src/Chamilo/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php and src/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php use paths supplied by an imported legacy course backup without consistently confining them to the extraction directory. A course teacher can import a crafted backup containing parent-directory path segments, causing file operations to write attacker-controlled content outside the intended destination, including PHP-executable or automatically loaded locations. This can result in code execution as the PHP process and compromise course data, user data, credentials, and the host. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the BigBlueButton plugin is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) injection when an authenticated administrator configures a malicious BigBlueButton server URL. Processing attacker-controlled XML from that server can read arbitrary local files and perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Sensitive configuration, credentials, source code, and internal network resources may be exposed. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

title: uftpd is a UNIX FTP and TFTP server.
desc: uftpd is a UNIX FTP and TFTP server. Prior to 2.16, uftpd's compose_path function in src/common.c can overflow the fixed dir[PATH_MAX] stack buffer when the server runs without chroot and prepends the configured home directory to a near-PATH_MAX attacker-supplied path using memmove. A logged-in FTP client, including an anonymous or guest client where enabled, can trigger the out-of-bounds write through commands such as CWD, RETR, STOR, or LIST, causing memory corruption and a reliable service crash. Remote code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 2.16.

title: mini-snmpd is a minimal SNMP agent implementation.
desc: mini-snmpd is a minimal SNMP agent implementation. Prior to 1.7, the ASN.1 BER parser in protocol.c does not verify that an attacker-controlled field length is no greater than the remaining packet size before decode_str(), decode_oid(), and decode_ptr() evaluate size - len + 1. When len exceeds size, unsigned size_t arithmetic wraps and bypasses the bounds check, allowing the decoder to read beyond the 2048-byte packet buffer. Parsing occurs before the SNMP community string is checked, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can send one crafted request to UDP port 161 to crash the process and potentially disclose adjacent heap memory. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.

title: Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems.
desc: Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems. From 5.4.8 until 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1, mint-refresh-cache passes a user-controlled --parent-window-id value directly to the privileged Synaptic process without validating it as an integer. A local user permitted to execute mint-refresh-cache through sudo can inject additional Synaptic command-line options and achieve arbitrary code execution as root. This issue is fixed in versions 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1.

title: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server.
desc:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) checked only that the caller was logged in, not the read_servers or manage_servers permission. Any authenticated user, including a user with no permissions, could download a diagnostic archive with the server log files, the host process list, a file system listing and the runtime server configuration. The runtime configuration contains the HTTP JWT signing secret and the message encryption key when they are set in the configuration. If HTTP is enabled, the user could use the signing secret to create tokens for any account, including root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: before 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

title: The Essential Real Estate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3 via deserialization of untrusted input in the…
desc: The Essential Real Estate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3 via deserialization of untrusted input in the 'saved_search_check_result' function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present.

title: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software.
desc: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the callsign parameter accepted by POST /oqrs/search_log in application/controllers/Oqrs.php search_log() reaches application/models/Oqrs_model.php search_log(), where it is concatenated directly into a raw SQL WHERE clause without parameter binding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use UNION-based SQL injection to read arbitrary application database records, including account data, password hashes, API keys, station credentials, reset tokens, QSO data, and station metadata. Disclosure of password reset tokens can be combined with the forgot_password workflow to take over accounts, including administrator accounts. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

title: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software.
desc: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. In 3.2.5 and earlier, the Hams of Note feature stores the administrator-supplied hon_url configuration value through application/controllers/Options.php hon_save() and application/models/Update_model.php update_hams_of_note() fetches that URL without restricting the scheme, host, loopback, link-local, or private network destinations. An administrator can cause the Wavelog server to request arbitrary HTTP or HTTPS destinations from its network position and have parsed response content rendered in the administrator interface, providing a read primitive against otherwise unreachable internal HTTP services. The HTTP status requirement prevents file scheme responses from succeeding, so this issue does not provide local file disclosure. No fixed version is available as of this review.

title: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software.
desc: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the filename parameter accepted by POST /qsl/addQsoToQsl in application/controllers/Qsl.php addQsoToQsl() is stored without rejecting directory separators or relative path components, and POST /qsl/delete reaches application/models/Qsl_model.php deleteQsl(), which passes the planted qsl_images filename to unlink(). A standard authenticated user can associate the malicious filename with the user's own QSO, satisfy the ownership check, escape the per-user QSL image directory, and delete files writable by the PHP worker. Deleting configuration or operational files can cause denial of service, while deleting installer gate files can reopen the unauthenticated installer and enable application identity takeover through attacker-controlled database configuration. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

title: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software.
desc: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 3.2.4, the application/controllers/Lotw.php import() workflow passes the lotw_download_url configuration value to curl without scheme validation, accepts file:// content, and writes the response to a predictable path under ./uploads/ that can be retrieved through an unauthenticated HTTP request. A standard user can trigger the LotW import, although changing lotw_download_url normally requires installer administrator access, and related vulnerabilities can remove that prerequisite. The same missing status-validation pattern affects the LotW lotw_users fetch helper and per-user download helper. This exposes files readable by the www-data user, including environment data, mounted secrets, and application configuration. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.4.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, POST /api/social_posts accepts attacker-controlled content that SocialPost::setContent stores without cross-site scripting sanitization, and assets/vue/components/social/SocialWallPost.vue renders post.content through v-html without sanitization. Any authenticated user can create a social-wall post that executes active content when another authenticated user views the wall. The script can run in an administrator's browser session and expose session data or perform actions with the victim's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, main/lp/scormItem.class.php and public/main/lp/scormItem.class.php store an attacker-controlled title element from imsmanifest.xml without cross-site scripting sanitization when a teacher imports a SCORM package. The title reaches c_lp_item.title and is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/LearnPath/scorm_list.html.twig through item.title with raw output while Twig auto-escaping is disabled; the default configuration does not apply the optional AI-disclosure sanitization path. Enrolled students or administrators who view the learning-path table of contents can execute the stored content in their browser sessions. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

title: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal.
desc: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, apps/dashboard/config/initializers/session_store.rb stores dashboard sessions by default in a predictable /var/tmp/<username> directory, or in another location configured by an administrator, but omits PUN user directory ownership and mode 0700 validation. A local attacker can pre-create another user's directory, read the victim's session identifier and CSRF token after login, or stage a predetermined session identifier. ActiveSupport file-store deserialization of attacker-controlled cache data may also occur in the victim's context, enabling file modification or code execution with the victim's privileges. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3.

title: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal.
desc: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to Open OnDemand 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, and prior to ood-ansible 4.2.1, the portal generator defaults OIDCCryptoPassphrase to SHA1(servername), and the templates/ood_portal.yml.j2 role checks a different variable from the documented passphrase setting. Administrators who set ood_oidc_crypto_passphrase can therefore believe a strong secret is configured while the deployment continues to use an attacker-derivable value. In OIDCSessionType client-cookie deployments, an unauthenticated remote attacker can derive the encryption key and forge a mod_auth_openidc_session cookie for another user, while server-cache deployments permit lower-impact tampering with protected OIDC state and nonce cookies. This issue is fixed in Open OnDemand versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3 and ood-ansible version 4.2.1.

title: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal.
desc: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, the Open OnDemand dashboard includes noVNC passwords in query parameters generated by apps/dashboard/app/helpers/batch_connect/sessions_helper.rb and apps/dashboard/app/views/batch_connect/sessions/connections/_novnc.html.erb. The server records those query strings in per-user PUN access logs, and insufficiently protected log directories can allow another local user to recover and replay a launch URL. Replaying the credential grants access to the running remote desktop and can result in horizontal or vertical privilege escalation according to the privileges of the desktop owner. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, public/main/course_description/course_description_controller.php assigns contentDescription directly from a teacher's request in the Doctrine-based add and edit paths without cross-site scripting sanitization. The stored value is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/Course/about.html.twig through description with raw output, and the /course/{id}/about route is publicly accessible. A teacher can store active content that executes when an authenticated or unauthenticated visitor views the course description, enabling session theft, credential phishing, defacement, or actions in an authenticated victim's session. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

title: The GLPI Inventory Plugin handles network discovery, inventory, software deployment, and data collection for GLPI agents.
desc: The GLPI Inventory Plugin handles network discovery, inventory, software deployment, and data collection for GLPI agents. Prior to 1.6.8, the /b/deploy, /b/collect, and /b/esx agent API endpoints do not authenticate requests before processing Deploy, Collect, and ESX task operations. An unauthenticated remote attacker can enumerate jobs and manipulate their status through these endpoints, disclosing job information and interfering with task processing. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.8.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
desc: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.1, main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php and public/main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php trust the request uid parameter instead of the authenticated user identity when saving SCORM learning objectives. Any authenticated student can replace uid with another user's identifier and overwrite that user's objectives because the endpoint performs no ownership check. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.1.

desc: The Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to incorrect authorization in all versions up to, and including, 6.7.0. title: A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0) allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading…
desc:
A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0)  allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) attack against the Airlock Gateway. The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1.

For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. The buffer overflow then happens during the parsing of that HTML response. Such a response can come either from a malicious or compromised backend, or from an otherwise trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, e.g. an application that stores and serves plain user-provided HTML files.

Successfully exploiting the vulnerability can enable an attacker to perform a DoS attack or, in the worst case, an RCE attack against the Airlock Gateway in front of the affected backend. Compromising the functionality of the Airlock Gateway could in this way also affect the availability and protection of other well-intentioned backends deployed behind the same Gateway.
