title: MISP contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Sighting model when the Sightings_anonymise setting is enabled.
desc: MISP contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Sighting model when the Sightings_anonymise setting is enabled. The listSightings and sightings/restSearch endpoints accepted a caller-supplied org_id filter parameter and applied it directly to the SQL query without verifying whether the requesting user was authorized to filter by that organisation. Because the anonymization mechanism masks the reporter's organisation in the returned records, a non-site-admin user could bypass the anonymization by specifying another organisation's ID in the filter. The query would then return only that organisation's sightings, effectively naming the reporter and defeating the purpose of the anonymization feature. A negated filter (NOT IN) similarly revealed which sightings belonged to the target organisation by exclusion. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with sighting read permissions (perm_sighting) who is not a site administrator, and the Sightings_anonymise plugin setting must be enabled. The security impact is the disclosure of which organisation reported a given sighting, undermining the privacy guarantees that the anonymization feature is designed to provide. This issue was reported by ENISA.

title: MISP contains an access control flaw in its tag management endpoints: events/addTag (single and bulk), events/removeTag, and attributes/removeTag.
desc: MISP contains an access control flaw in its tag management endpoints: events/addTag (single and bulk), events/removeTag, and attributes/removeTag. These endpoints loaded their target event or attribute using an unscoped database query (recursive = -1) that did not apply the calling user's ACL visibility rules. As a result, two distinct security issues existed: (1) Information disclosure: the removeTag endpoint returned different responses depending on whether a given tag was present on a hidden event, allowing an authenticated user to enumerate which tags were applied to events they had no visibility into. (2) Unauthorized modification: users belonging to the host organisation, who are permitted to set local tags on records they can see, could add or remove local tags on events and attributes they could not see, because the canModifyTag ACL check operated on the unscoped object without first verifying the caller's visibility. The fix replaces the unscoped find() calls with ACL-aware fetch methods (fetchSimpleEvent and fetchAttributeSimple) that apply the user's visibility before the object is returned, and adds an explicit empty-object check in removeTag so that a hidden event responds identically to a non-existent one. Affected components include the EventsController (addTag, removeTag), the AttributesController (removeTag), and the ACLComponent (canModifyTag). The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with at least the tagger role (perm_tagger) or host-organisation membership.

title: MISP's EventDelegationsController delegateEvent method accepted a user-supplied sharing_group_id parameter without verifying that the requesting user was a member of the…
desc: MISP's EventDelegationsController delegateEvent method accepted a user-supplied sharing_group_id parameter without verifying that the requesting user was a member of the referenced sharing group. When a delegation request was submitted with distribution set to 4 (sharing-group distribution), the raw sharing_group_id value was stored directly into the EventDelegation record. The delegation view subsequently rendered the stored sharing group's name back to the requester. Because no authorization check was performed, any authenticated user with delegation permission could enumerate sharing group identifiers (by guessing sequential IDs or other values) and read the names of sharing groups to which their organisation did not belong, including hidden or restricted groups. Hidden, missing, and malformed identifiers were not distinguished in the response, but the successful case still leaked the group name. The vulnerability required an authenticated session with the perm_delegate capability and knowledge of a valid event ID to delegate. The security impact is limited to disclosure of sharing group names (a low-impact confidentiality breach) and does not grant access to the group's contents or modify any data.

title: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the correlations/eventCorrelations endpoint and the underlying correlation engines (Default and OnDemand).
desc: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the correlations/eventCorrelations endpoint and the underlying correlation engines (Default and OnDemand). The CorrelationsController::eventCorrelations action did not verify that the requesting user was permitted to view the event specified by the event ID parameter. Any authenticated user could supply the ID of an event belonging to another organisation (distribution level 0, organisation-only) and receive its full correlation results, including attribute identifiers and values. Additionally, for events the user could partially view, the correlation engines filtered only the related (target) side of each correlation row and did not vet the queried event's own source attributes. As a result, correlations keyed by attributes hidden from the user (organisation-only attributes, attributes in sharing groups the user is not a member of, or attributes inside organisation-only objects) were returned with their IDs and values. The Default engine's related-event listing (used in events/view) also included events related solely through such hidden attributes. The vulnerability was reported by ENISA. Successful exploitation requires a valid authenticated session with any role and knowledge or enumeration of a target event ID. The security impact is disclosure of threat-intelligence attribute values (IP addresses, domain names, etc.) and attribute identifiers that the user is not authorised to see, as well as confirmation of the existence of otherwise invisible events.

title: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its event search and filter functionality.
desc:
MISP contains an authorization bypass in its event search and filter functionality. When a user performed searches through events/restSearch (value, value prefix, searchall, type, uuid, attribute tags, object filters), objects/restSearch, or the event index tag, galaxy, and quick filters, the underlying SQL subqueries matched against attributes and objects without enforcing the per-attribute distribution, sharing-group, or soft-deleted visibility rules that apply when fetching individual elements.

A user who could view an event (for example, a community-distributed event) could therefore use search to determine whether organisation-only, sharing-group-restricted, or soft-deleted attributes and objects existed within that event. Because the value filter supports prefix matching (LIKE), an attacker could enumerate the full value of a hidden attribute one character at a time. Tags attached exclusively to hidden attributes also leaked through the tag, galaxy, and quick-filter paths on the event index.

The vulnerability affects the EventsController quick-filter and index-filter logic, the Event model wildcard/value/uuid/tag filter methods, the MispAttribute tag filter, the MispObject buildFilterConditions and restSearch methods, and the ReportFromEvent object filter. Site administrators and users belonging to the event's own organisation retain full visibility, and sync users continue to match soft-deleted elements as intended.

The issue was reported by ENISA.

title: When payload encryption is enabled, failure messages and stack traces that temporal-proxy is configured to keep from the upstream Temporal service can reach it in plaintext…
desc: When payload encryption is enabled, failure messages and stack traces that temporal-proxy is configured to keep from the upstream Temporal service can reach it in plaintext, where anyone who can read the Workflow's history at the upstream can read them. When the proxy returns a failure to a Worker, it decrypts the failure's encoded attributes and copies the message and stack trace back onto the failure, keeping the attributes. A Worker that sends that failure back through the proxy, as SDKs do when an Activity failure becomes the cause of a Workflow failure, sends the restored text with it, and the proxy forwards the text unchanged because the failure already has encoded attributes. The upstream then stores the text in plaintext beside its encrypted copy. This affects deployments that enable failure encryption in the proxy, and deployments that leave it off while the SDK encodes failure attributes itself. Payloads are not affected. temporal-proxy versions 0.9.0 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.

title: A flaw was found in the file-xmc plugin in GIMP.
desc: A flaw was found in the file-xmc plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted XMC image file, the plugin does not properly validate the comment subtype before using it as an array index. This missing validation leads to out-of-bounds memory access, invalid free and use-after-free issues. This vulnerability can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

title: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the user login-email change logic.
desc: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the user login-email change logic. When an external authentication backend is configured (LDAP, Shibboleth, ApacheSecureAuth, or CustomAuth), the login email address serves as the key by which the directory service resolves a user's identity, organization, and role on each login. The __canChangeLogin() method in UsersController only checked the MISP.disable_user_login_change setting and site-admin status; it did not account for whether an external authentication backend was active. As a result, any authenticated non-admin user (including org admins) could change their own login email to an address that matches a higher-privilege account in the external directory. On the user's next login, the external backend would resolve that email to the target directory identity, granting the attacker the organization and role associated with that identity. This constitutes an account-identity capture and privilege escalation: the attacker effectively assumes the identity of any directory account whose email they can guess or discover. The vulnerability requires an authenticated session with a valid API key or session token and a MISP instance configured with at least one external authentication backend. The impact is limited to the scope of the captured directory identity's privileges within MISP.

title: A security vulnerability has been detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6.
desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file mainfunction.cgi of the component Apmcfg Upload. The manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 addresses this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

title: A weakness has been identified in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6.
desc: A weakness has been identified in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. Affected is the function setSWMProfile of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi. Executing a manipulation of the argument filename can lead to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to address this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

desc: A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing authentication requests using the Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes the server process to crash before validating authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

desc: Weblate 5.0 through 2026.11.2 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability where deleting a component list leaves stale Group.projects rows, widening team scope to whole projects. Attackers can open the /message WebSocket from a victim's browser, even against localhost-bound gateways, to initialize an MCP session and invoke wrapped stdio MCP server tools with victim privileges.

title: Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK.
desc:
Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for.

This issue affects Apache Iggy Go SDK: from 0.5.0 before 0.10.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their long expiry on the server. Delete those tokens and create new ones.

title: MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method.
desc:
MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method. The authorization check used a logical AND condition that effectively exempted users with the sync permission (perm_sync) from the membership verification. Specifically, the original condition 'if (!checkIfAuthorised(...) && !perm_sync) return false' meant that any user holding the sync role would pass the check regardless of whether they were actually a member of the target sharing group.

A sync user who knows or can discover the UUID of a non-local sharing group could exploit this flaw through the /sharing_groups/add endpoint or by embedding a SharingGroup object in pushed sync data. The attacker could rewrite the sharing group record to add their own organisation as a member or insert an all_orgs server entry for their MISP instance, thereby gaining read access to all events contained in that group. This exposes threat intelligence data that was intended to be restricted to the group's legitimate members.

The vulnerability requires an authenticated account with the sync role and knowledge of a valid sharing group UUID. No user interaction is required. The impact is unauthorized disclosure of shared threat intelligence events and limited integrity modification of the sharing group record.

title: A flaw was found in lldpd.
desc: A flaw was found in lldpd. The service fails to verify that Link Layer Discovery Protocol - Media Endpoint Discovery (LLDP-MED) location records received from network neighbors match their declared lengths. An adjacent attacker on the local network can exploit this flaw by sending crafted packets, causing client applications using the liblldpctl library to read past buffer boundaries when parsing location data. This issue can lead to an information disclosure of adjacent process memory.

title: Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster…
desc:
Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster initialised via msfdb init is configured with trust authentication and a world-accessible Unix domain socket in /tmp, allowing any local user on the same host to authenticate as the passwordless postgres superuser and execute arbitrary operating system commands as the msfdb owner. 


This issue is fixed in version 6.5.10.

desc: GNU Emacs 31.1 contains a code injection vulnerability in its handling of directory-local variables. A crafted .dir-locals.el can supply a (REGEXP FUNCTION t) entry in auto-mode-alist; when a matching file is opened, Emacs calls FUNCTION before set-auto-mode--dir-local-valid-p validates it, executing arbitrary Emacs Lisp with the privileges of the Emacs process. (Emacs 30.2 is unaffected.)

desc: WLA DX 9.7 through 10.7 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in parse_data_blocks() in wlalink/analyze.c that copies section namespaces without length checks. desc: Pika before 1.5.0 contains an uncontrolled resource allocation vulnerability that allows malicious brokers to exhaust client memory by declaring oversized frame payloads. This vulnerability affected all versions prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, and 3.20.12. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an organization member with permission to manage custom-property definitions…
desc: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an organization member with permission to manage custom-property definitions and edit property values to add an attacker-controlled SSH authentication key to the personal account of another member through HTML stored in a single-select custom-property option. Exploitation required another definition manager in the same organization to attempt to remove the poisoned option while it was in use and save the definition with a valid sudo session. Repository access through the added key depended on the permissions of the victim and independent authorization controls. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: A CRLF injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a user with write access to a repository to bypass branch protections and update branches…
desc: A CRLF injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a user with write access to a repository to bypass branch protections and update branches or tags in that repository through specially crafted input when resolving pull request conflicts. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Igor Funa Ad Inserter ad-inserter allows Code Injection.This issue affects Ad…
desc: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Igor Funa Ad Inserter ad-inserter allows Code Injection.This issue affects Ad Inserter: from n/a through 2.8.19.

title: Finsys Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users with stacks:edit permission to move arbitrary server directories by supplying a crafted…
desc: Finsys Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users with stacks:edit permission to move arbitrary server directories by supplying a crafted oldDir parameter. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/stacks/[name]/relocate with an unvalidated source path to relocate directories into stack paths, disrupting services and exposing their contents.

title: SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup…
desc: SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup reference names in MediaWiki:Smw_allows_pattern. Once an editor annotates the matching Allows pattern value, AllowsPatternValue emits it unescaped on Special:Browse, executing JavaScript in every viewer's session.

title: SemanticMediaWiki from 7.3.0 before 7.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the smwtask API check-query task that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass…
desc: SemanticMediaWiki from 7.3.0 before 7.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the smwtask API check-query task that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass object-level authorization by relying on the wiki-wide edit right. Attackers can supply arbitrary subject titles, including protected pages, to run synchronous Semantic MediaWiki queries with caller-controlled conditions, limit, offset, and querymode parameters.

title: SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in CsvFileExportPrinter and DsvResultPrinter via unescaped valuesep and…
desc: SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in CsvFileExportPrinter and DsvResultPrinter via unescaped valuesep and separator parameters. Attackers can craft Special:Ask links using request_type=special_page so export output renders as text/html, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers under the wiki origin.

title: Frappe ERPNext before 16.35.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in financial reporting endpoints that allows low-privilege authenticated users to generate reports…
desc: Frappe ERPNext before 16.35.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in financial reporting endpoints that allows low-privilege authenticated users to generate reports outside their permitted scope. Attackers can send crafted requests to affected reporting endpoints to read other companies' tax and payment data, including personal and corporate identifiers and financial totals.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows users who can launch instances from controlled images to inject LXC directives by embedding line…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows users who can launch instances from controlled images to inject LXC directives by embedding line breaks in OCI config.json values or oci.entrypoint and oci.cwd keys. Attackers can add liblxc hooks or crafted tmpfs lxc.mount.entry fields to run commands as root on the host or bind-mount host paths, even from restricted projects.

title: Incus from 7.3.0 before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest API that allows a process in one container to impersonate another by…
desc: Incus from 7.3.0 before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest API that allows a process in one container to impersonate another by creating a cgroup named with a forged lxc.monitor. component. Attackers can read the target container's user.* and cloud-init.* configuration and devices, subscribe to its events, mark it ready, and export images across projects.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted clients to create and access default project resources by exploiting entitlement checks…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted clients to create and access default project resources by exploiting entitlement checks against the requested project. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq directives to execute code as root on the host, or manipulate inherited resources via the ?project= parameter.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 exposes certificate and cluster join token secrets through the default project event stream and skips authorization when cancelling operations without…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 exposes certificate and cluster join token secrets through the default project event stream and skips authorization when cancelling operations without associated permissions. Restricted clients can subscribe to operation events to capture certificate tokens and enroll unrestricted certificates, gaining full server access, or cancel token operations by UUID.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted and view-only clients to read default project resources by requesting the default…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted and view-only clients to read default project resources by requesting the default project directly. Attackers knowing resource names can read profiles, images, network zone peer keys and stored credentials, and export custom volume or bucket backups to obtain full contents or S3 admin keys.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the storage bucket S3 listener, which buffers entire signed request bodies in memory before verifying the…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the storage bucket S3 listener, which buffers entire signed request bodies in memory before verifying the signature or credential role. Attackers knowing only a valid access key, or holding a read-only credential, can send many concurrent large requests to exhaust daemon memory.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious migration peers to write outside intended directories by supplying unvalidated dependent volume…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious migration peers to write outside intended directories by supplying unvalidated dependent volume and snapshot names in the migration offer header. Attackers controlling a migration source can create root-owned volumes with attacker content at arbitrary host paths, compromising hosts using dir storage pools, bypassing restricted.storage-pools.access, or crashing the daemon.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users permitted to import custom volumes to store unvalidated snapshot names from the backup index…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users permitted to import custom volumes to store unvalidated snapshot names from the backup index configuration section. Attackers can craft a backup with traversal sequences in snapshot names so later deletion removes arbitrary host directories as root, while renaming or mounting operates on arbitrary paths.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to authenticate as any trusted certificate by appending its public certificate to…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to authenticate as any trusted certificate by appending its public certificate to their presented TLS client chain. Attackers can append the server's or a cluster member's certificate to gain cluster-level access, bypass authorization, modify trust store entries, and influence scriptlet-based authorization decisions.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project-restricted authenticated clients to receive other projects' OVN ACL logs because these…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project-restricted authenticated clients to receive other projects' OVN ACL logs because these events are broadcast with an empty project. Attackers can subscribe to network-acl events on one accessible project to observe internal IPs, ports, protocols, and allow/drop decisions across all projects.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients with project event-view access to read migration websocket secrets broadcast in operation…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients with project event-view access to read migration websocket secrets broadcast in operation metadata. Attackers can connect to in-flight migration control and fs websockets before the legitimate peer, hijacking the transfer to obtain instance configuration and filesystem data.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest-API image export handler that fails to pin the project parameter to the guest's own…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest-API image export handler that fails to pin the project parameter to the guest's own project. Container root users with the guest-API image entitlement can supply another project in the project query parameter to export public or cached images, including non-public images pulled from authenticated remotes.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability: rebuilding a never-started unprivileged container makes it boot without a user namespace.
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability: rebuilding a never-started unprivileged container makes it boot without a user namespace. Root processes inside the container run as host uid 0, keeping capabilities like sys_module, with no device cgroup restriction, letting them load kernel modules and compromise the host.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows restricted project users to create resources in the unrestricted default project by targeting projects lacking…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows restricted project users to create resources in the unrestricted default project by targeting projects lacking features.* flags. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq dhcp-script injection to run scripts as root, or custom volumes with block.create_options mkfs arguments to read host files.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted TLS clients to read other projects' bucket S3 keys and profile configuration through…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted TLS clients to read other projects' bucket S3 keys and profile configuration through recursive and all-projects responses. Attackers can query bucket listings with recursion=2 or profiles with all-projects=true to obtain S3 secret keys and sensitive environment, cloud-init and user values across projects.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 fails to reject special files, hard links, or symlinks in backup or image metadata, allowing restricted project users to read or overwrite host files.
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 fails to reject special files, hard links, or symlinks in backup or image metadata, allowing restricted project users to read or overwrite host files. Attackers can import crafted backups containing device nodes, a hard-linked backup.yaml, or symlinks to corrupt host storage, overwrite host files, or leak other projects' data.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 creates the NBD servers used for virtual machine migration and disk export on abstract unix sockets, which have no permission checks and whose names are…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 creates the NBD servers used for virtual machine migration and disk export on abstract unix sockets, which have no permission checks and whose names are visible in /proc/net/unix. A local unprivileged user can connect while an operation runs to read or modify the VM disk, gaining code execution in the guest on a migration's receiving side.

title: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows clients permitted to create instances to crash the daemon by importing a backup with a null snapshot…
desc: Incus before 7.6.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows clients permitted to create instances to crash the daemon by importing a backup with a null snapshot entry in index.yaml. Attackers can trigger an unrecovered nil pointer dereference during configuration rewrite, terminating the daemon and all containers and virtual machines on the node.

title: Obot from 0.14.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power Users to bypass outbound protections by supplying unspecified addresses…
desc: Obot from 0.14.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power Users to bypass outbound protections by supplying unspecified addresses, IPv6 transition addresses, or registry icon URLs. Attackers can add remote MCP servers pointing to 0.0.0.0, ::, or NAT64/6to4/Teredo addresses embedding blocked IPv4 addresses to probe internal services for reachability.

title: Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP…
desc: Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.

title: Obot from 0.26.0 before 0.27.0 fails to validate the resource identifier in remote MCP server protected resource metadata, allowing malicious MCP servers to steal access tokens.
desc: Obot from 0.26.0 before 0.27.0 fails to validate the resource identifier in remote MCP server protected resource metadata, allowing malicious MCP servers to steal access tokens. Attackers can name a different service and authorization server with chosen scopes, causing Obot to obtain the victim's token for that service and forward it to the attacker.

title: Obot before 0.27.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass same-site validation of the rd parameter by inserting a tab character.
desc: Obot before 0.27.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass same-site validation of the rd parameter by inserting a tab character. Attackers can craft sign-in or sign-out links on the Obot domain that browsers resolve to external hosts, redirecting victims to phishing pages.

title: Obot from 0.8.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power User accounts to reach internal hosts by advertising a malicious OAuth token…
desc: Obot from 0.8.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power User accounts to reach internal hosts by advertising a malicious OAuth token endpoint in remote MCP server metadata. Attackers can direct token exchange or refresh requests, including redirected GET requests, to cloud metadata services or private-network hosts and read error response bodies.

title: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in the host inventory export endpoint that allows attackers controlling an enrolled host or enroll secret to…
desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in the host inventory export endpoint that allows attackers controlling an enrolled host or enroll secret to plant spreadsheet formulas. Attackers can set osquery-reported fields like hostname or hardware serial to formula values, enabling data exfiltration or DDE command execution when users open the exported CSV.

title: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated observer-level users to sort software listings by arbitrary columns via the order_key…
desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated observer-level users to sort software listings by arbitrary columns via the order_key parameter. Attackers can order by joined hosts table columns such as node keys and use pagination as a binary-search oracle to extract sensitive column values.

title: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows enrolled hosts to trigger unbounded per-name database lookups by submitting osquery result logs.
desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows enrolled hosts to trigger unbounded per-name database lookups by submitting osquery result logs. Attackers with a valid host node key can send one request to /api/osquery/log containing many distinct query names, exhausting database connections and read replica capacity.

title: Fleet before 4.86.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via unbounded BER recursion in PKCS#7 parsing.
desc: Fleet before 4.86.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via unbounded BER recursion in PKCS#7 parsing. Attackers can send deeply nested indefinite-length structures to Apple MDM check-in, enrollment, SCEP, or OTA endpoints to crash the entire Fleet instance.

title: Fleet from 4.71.0 before 4.88.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SAML SSO callback that looks up sessions using unvalidated client-supplied identifiers.
desc: Fleet from 4.71.0 before 4.88.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SAML SSO callback that looks up sessions using unvalidated client-supplied identifiers. Users able to run live queries or enroll secret holders can plant attacker-controlled identity provider metadata in the session store, then present a self-signed SAML response to log in as a global admin.

title: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the deprecated POST /api/latest/fleet/mdm/apple/enqueue endpoint that allows team-scoped users to enqueue…
desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the deprecated POST /api/latest/fleet/mdm/apple/enqueue endpoint that allows team-scoped users to enqueue Apple MDM commands outside their teams. Attackers with team admin, maintainer, or GitOps roles can include one own-team host UUID alongside unresolved enrollment IDs to send commands like InstallProfile to deleted or user-channel enrollments without activity logging.

title: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse case-mutated security tokens because MySQL token columns used…
desc: Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse case-mutated security tokens because MySQL token columns used case-insensitive collation. Attackers holding a case-normalized invite or email-change token can redirect a victim's email for account takeover or redeem invites with roles up to Global Admin.

title: pnpm exe before 10.34.8 embeds an outdated Node.js runtime that still trusts compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates during registry TLS connections.
desc: pnpm exe before 10.34.8 embeds an outdated Node.js runtime that still trusts compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates during registry TLS connections. Network attackers holding a recovered intermediate key can intercept standalone pnpm registry fetches and serve forged package metadata or tarballs.

title: Froxlor before 2.3.16 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to read hidden traffic statistics by calling the Traffic.listing API…
desc: Froxlor before 2.3.16 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to read hidden traffic statistics by calling the Traffic.listing API command. Attackers can authenticate to api.php with their API key and secret to retrieve HTTP, FTP, and mail traffic volumes despite the panel.customer_hide_options restriction.

title: All versions of LaraDashboard contain an authentication bypass in SocialAuthService::findOrCreateUser(), which links a social login to an existing account by email without…
desc: All versions of LaraDashboard contain an authentication bypass in SocialAuthService::findOrCreateUser(), which links a social login to an existing account by email without checking that the OAuth provider verified that email. Unauthenticated attackers using an OAuth/OIDC provider that asserts a victim's email can log in as any user, including Superadmin, and keep persistent access through a linked social_accounts entry.

title: heym before 0.0.142 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Playwright step-mode node where _resolve_expressions_in_code substitutes workflow values directly into…
desc: heym before 0.0.142 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Playwright step-mode node where _resolve_expressions_in_code substitutes workflow values directly into generated Python source. Authenticated non-admin users can craft step field values that break out of string literals to execute arbitrary Python as root inside the backend container.

title: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-uhttpd before commit d38658bedbdd811b798da16b49301478c6cf21af grants '/*' file read in its rpcd read ACL, which rpcd's fnmatch matching applies to every path.
desc: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-uhttpd before commit d38658bedbdd811b798da16b49301478c6cf21af grants '/*' file read in its rpcd read ACL, which rpcd's fnmatch matching applies to every path. Users delegated only luci-app-uhttpd read access can read any file as root, including /etc/shadow, /etc/config/* credentials, /etc/uhttpd.key, and /etc/dropbear keys.

title: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-travelmate on master before 3.0.0-1, on openwrt-25.12 before 2.4.9-6, and on openwrt-24.10 and openwrt-23.05 (no fix available) grants file exec permissions…
desc: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-travelmate on master before 3.0.0-1, on openwrt-25.12 before 2.4.9-6, and on openwrt-24.10 and openwrt-23.05 (no fix available) grants file exec permissions for state-mutating commands in the read scope of its rpcd ACL, letting authenticated read-only users run those commands as root. Attackers can invoke ubus file exec on /etc/init.d/travelmate setup, start, stop, restart, or /sbin/ifup to modify and commit network and firewall configuration or disrupt the travelmate daemon.

title: Network-AI from 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 contains a CORS misconfiguration in McpStreamableServer that reflects localhost Origins into Access-Control-Allow-Origin regardless of bind…
desc: Network-AI from 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 contains a CORS misconfiguration in McpStreamableServer that reflects localhost Origins into Access-Control-Allow-Origin regardless of bind interface. Attackers controlling a localhost-origin page or DNS-rebinding name can read unauthenticated /tools and /health responses, exposing tool catalogs and bridge metadata on non-loopback binds.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to fill the disk by varying the HTTP Host header.
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to fill the disk by varying the HTTP Host header. Attackers can send requests with distinct Host values to create per-host compiled configuration, blueprint, language and page index caches, causing session, upload and logging failures.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to redirect reset links by forging the CloudFront-Forwarded-Proto…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to redirect reset links by forging the CloudFront-Forwarded-Proto header. Attackers can send a forgot-password request with a crafted scheme value so the emailed reset link points to their host, capturing the token to take over accounts including super admins.

title: Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to create super-admin accounts because…
desc: Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to create super-admin accounts because UserCollection::count() uses an unescaped glob() pattern. On installs whose path contains brackets or a backslash, the account count returns zero, so attackers can send requests to POST /api/v1/auth/setup or the classic admin registration form to create or overwrite administrator accounts.

title: Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 serves page media files, and rendered pages when lazy sessions are enabled, with the visitor's session cookie and a shared-cacheable…
desc: Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 serves page media files, and rendered pages when lazy sessions are enabled, with the visitor's session cookie and a shared-cacheable Cache-Control header. When a shared cache such as Apache mod_cache stores Set-Cookie responses, an attacker can lure a user signed in through the front-end login to open a media URL with a unique query string, then request that URL to receive the cached session cookie and take over the session.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page cache key. Routine editor activity through the API plugin rebuilds the page index without frontmatter.yaml access rules, exposing members-only page content until the cache is rebuilt.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows page editors to escape the Twig sandbox by sending requests with a Host: pages header.
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows page editors to escape the Twig sandbox by sending requests with a Host: pages header. Attackers can write configuration YAML through page folders and media .meta.yaml sidecars to register an unsandboxed Twig namespace and run shell commands as the web server user.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

title: Grav 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 resolves Flex sort and filter field names by first calling them as public methods, so a field named delete invokes FlexObject::delete() without any…
desc: Grav 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 resolves Flex sort and filter field names by first calling them as public methods, so a field named delete invokes FlexObject::delete() without any permission check. Authenticated users with only list access can send GET /api/v1/flex-objects/user-accounts?sort=delete requests to delete every account, then use the reopened API first-run setup to create a super admin.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig sandbox bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to read any server file by abusing allowlisted array_key_value() and page…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig sandbox bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to read any server file by abusing allowlisted array_key_value() and page accessor setters such as filePath(). Attackers can repoint page objects or overwrite the assets collections to render private keys and the API signing secret, then forge a super-admin API token.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows publishers and read-only user managers to read password hashes, 2FA secrets and reset…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows publishers and read-only user managers to read password hashes, 2FA secrets and reset tokens through unfiltered account serialization. Attackers can embed a Flex form for the user-accounts directory in a page or query the Flex API with admin.users.read to obtain super admin credentials and take over the account.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers and Flex editors to overwrite, create, or delete accounts by supplying…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers and Flex editors to overwrite, create, or delete accounts by supplying client-controlled storage keys. Attackers can abuse the create form username, cross-type form flash replay, or __META storage key rename to gain super-admin accounts or delete account files.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers with admin.users.update to take over super admin accounts by disabling the…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers with admin.users.update to take over super admin accounts by disabling the super-granting group. Attackers can set the group's enabled field to false via the Flex user-groups form, then reset the victim's password through the user-accounts form to gain super admin access.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers to grant super-admin rights by nesting access maps under a YAML merge key.
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers to grant super-admin rights by nesting access maps under a YAML merge key. Attackers with admin.users.create or api.users.write can submit '<<' keys, for example via PATCH /api/v1/users/<self>, that bypass super-grant filtering and gain full site control.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers to bypass the media action allowlist using scoped method names in Markdown…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers to bypass the media action allowlist using scoped method names in Markdown image URLs. Attackers can chain actions like self::addMetaFile into static calls such as Process::fromShellCommandline to read files and run shell commands as the web server user.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image titles, alt text, class, id, or file names. Attackers can combine injected Twig with the autoescape tag to serve script to every page visitor, including super admins, or expose unpublished page content.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer.
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer. Attackers can upload SVG files with inner extensions like .svg.defaults, payloads that crash the fail-open sanitizer, or unblocked .xml/.xhtm files to run script when administrators open the raw file URL.

title: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage…
desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage key delimiter collisions and PageStorage folder reconstruction. Attackers can rename a folder like locked*** or save from a page with an unusual prefix width through a front-end Flex pages form, replacing protected content and permissions to access the protected subtree.

title: Traefik from 2.11.58 before 2.11.61 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust resources by sending Authorization headers with NTLM…
desc: Traefik from 2.11.58 before 2.11.61 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust resources by sending Authorization headers with NTLM or Negotiate schemes. Attackers can open many short-lived connections that each allocate a dedicated backend transport never released, exhausting memory, file descriptors and backend connections.

title: NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the instance JWT secret. Attackers can present a narrowly scoped OAuth token to the session strategy, short-lived-token exchange, or NocoSocket handshake to gain the granting user's full privileges.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's row filters. Unauthenticated attackers holding a public share link can supply guessable auto-incrementing ids of filtered-out records to has-many, many-to-many, one-many, or link endpoints to read their child records.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to register OAuth clients with javascript: redirect URIs.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to register OAuth clients with javascript: redirect URIs. Attackers can send a consent link to a signed-in victim so either consent button runs script in the NocoDB origin, stealing the session token for account takeover.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.

title: NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements without numeric validation. Authenticated users with the Creator or Owner base role can supply a crafted precision value when creating or updating a column to close the type declaration and execute arbitrary SQL against the base's data source.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by storing foreign attachment paths in their own rows via prepareNocoData. Attackers with write access to an attachment column can have _convertAttachmentType or the attachment download endpoint sign the foreign path, reading cross-base files despite secure attachment mode.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to the integration remote fetch operation. Attackers can control the method, headers, and body to reach internal APIs, loopback services, and cloud metadata endpoints, reading responses and echoed decrypted integration secrets.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared view attachment-download endpoint. Attackers holding a public share link can enumerate sequential primary keys to obtain signed download paths for files on records the view's row filter excludes.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in shared-view relation endpoints because parent-record lookups apply only the primary key, not the view's row filter.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in shared-view relation endpoints because parent-record lookups apply only the primary key, not the view's row filter. Anonymous share-link holders can enumerate auto-increment primary keys against the has-many, many-to-many, one-to-many and link-to-another-record routes to read linked records of filtered-out rows.

title: NocoDB from 2026.06.2 before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to write to data-read-only sources by abusing the…
desc: NocoDB from 2026.06.2 before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to write to data-read-only sources by abusing the internal batch endpoint. Attackers can name a writable decoy table on the batch envelope and target a read-only source table in dataUpdate, dataInsert or dataDelete sub-operations to modify or destroy records.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access records hidden by a shared view's row filter by…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access records hidden by a shared view's row filter by supplying arbitrary primary keys. Attackers with the share link can request attachment downloads and many-to-many or has-many link listings for excluded records to obtain their attachment files and linked record identities.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through the general base metadata endpoint. Attackers with a share link can query the base read or list responses in bases.controller.ts, which skip password stripping in sanitizeBase.ts, to obtain reusable plaintext passwords.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because the read-by-primary-key path ignores the view's filters. Attackers can request the public attachment-download or nested-link listing routes with a record id to mint signed download URLs for hidden files and read linked-record data.

title: NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid. Attackers holding an unexpired reset link, such as from prior mailbox access, can set a new password and regain control of the account.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up endpoint responses. Attackers can submit addresses to signup in users.service.ts and compare error messages to identify existing accounts and pending Enterprise invitations, even under invite-only signup.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated Creators to access another tenant's external database by reusing a victim source…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated Creators to access another tenant's external database by reusing a victim source id when adding a source. Because NcConnectionMgrv2 caches connections by bare source id, attackers can reflect the victim's cached database schema and read, update, and insert records through their own base models.

title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator. Unauthenticated attackers with a job id can read buffered status messages and completion payloads, exposing signed export download URLs or new base identifiers.

title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars webhook helpers. Attackers can supply property paths like constructor.constructor to pluck, sortBy, filter, or withSort helpers to reach the Function constructor and run operating-system commands.

title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook plugin listing endpoint. Attackers can replay exposed Slack, Teams, Discord and Mattermost webhook URLs directly against messaging providers to post arbitrary messages into organization chat channels.

title: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute.
desc: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree reused without revalidation. Attackers can bypass the SQLite metadata path guard with an alias to plant the tree, escalating to super administrator or executing OS commands on external PostgreSQL hosts.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared view link holders to read hidden columns by grouping on physical…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared view link holders to read hidden columns by grouping on physical column names. Attackers can supply a hidden column's physical name or the unchecked sub-group parameter to the public group-by endpoint to reveal hidden values, counts, and column existence.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows Creator-role users to attach NocoDB's internal database by supplying is_meta and is_local…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows Creator-role users to attach NocoDB's internal database by supplying is_meta and is_local flags. Attackers can create sources or bases with these flags to expose user, token and integration tables, then read and modify records including user roles.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column lists. Attackers with a shared view link can pair a visible and hidden column to bypass restrictSharedViewColumnReferences and retrieve hidden values tied to individual rows.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations.
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations. Attackers can trigger baseUserInviteResend to mint a new invite_token, read it from the base member list, and reset the victim's password through signup, taking over owner or super admin accounts.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a consent phishing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register OAuth clients with arbitrary HTTPS redirect URIs through the…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a consent phishing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register OAuth clients with arbitrary HTTPS redirect URIs through the unauthenticated dynamic client registration endpoint. Attackers can impersonate trusted applications on a consent screen lacking unverified-client warnings or redirect host display, obtaining tokens to read and write victim tables and records.

title: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the…
desc: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting them through the session header. Attackers can bypass revocation, client-existence, route allowlist and granted_resources scope checks to modify victim profiles, upload to storage, and force global sign-outs.

title: NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the…
desc: NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the DATETIME_FORMAT formula format argument on MySQL-backed bases. Attackers can place a backslash before a quote to terminate the DATE_FORMAT string literal and read any data reachable by the data source's database user, including tables outside the base.

title: NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a…
desc: NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form property paths to Handlebars helpers in webhook templates. Attackers can bypass the string-only prototype guard to reach the function constructor, running operating-system commands with server privileges or exfiltrating process-internal values via outbound requests.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows organization Creators to reach routes restricted to other roles because the aclFn middleware…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows organization Creators to reach routes restricted to other roles because the aclFn middleware never enforced allowedRoles. Attackers can generate a super admin password reset link via org-users endpoints to take over the instance, or read and modify SSO client secrets.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree during table creation. Attackers can set a malicious binary-expression operator that is interpolated into a knex.raw fragment, reading user and token tables and escalating to super administrator on SQLite installs.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in…
desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

title: vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one…
desc: vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.

title: vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range…
desc: vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.

title: vLLM before 0.33.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious model publishers to redirect the served model and tokenizer by setting speculators_config…
